english.title: Supply regulated explosives precursor to business customer without being satisfied of their trade, business, profession
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) supplied regulated explosives precursor, namely **(..SPECIFY PRECURSOR..), to a business customer, namely **(..SPECIFY CUSTOMER..), without first being reasonably satisfied that acquisition of that precursor by that business customer was reasonably consistent with the nature of the customer’s trade, business or profession, or of the public function that the business customer performed
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 3(1) and (3) of the Control of Explosives Precursors and Poisons Regulations 2023 and sections 7(4) and 8(5) of the Poisons Act 1972.

english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant supplied a regulated explosives precursor, namely **(..SPECIFY PRECURSOR..), to a business customer, namely **(..SPECIFY CUSTOMER..), without first being reasonably satisfied that acquisition of that precursor by that business customer was reasonably consistent with the nature of the customer’s trade, business or profession, or of the public function that the business customer performed.

other.penalty:
Summary: a fine not exceeding level four on the standard scale.

In the case of a continuing offence, a further fine not exceeding one-tenth of level 4 on the standard scale for every day subsequent to the day on which the person is convicted of the offence during which the contravention or default continues.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Proceedings may be commenced at any time -
(a) within the period of 12 months next after the date of commission of the offence, or
(b) in the case of proceedings instituted by, or by the direction of, the Secretary of State, within the later to end of -
(i) that 12-month period, and (ii) the period of 3 months next after the date on which evidence sufficient in the Secretary of State's opinion to justify a prosecution for the offence comes to the Secretary of State's knowledge.
